title: Account ask skeletonization and initial solution sketch
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Purpose: Provide a lightweight, repeatable process to convert Sales/CS enterprise asks into a concise 'skeletonized' request plus an initial solution sketch that enables fast prioritization and an engineering feasibility check. This ticket defines the process, the required template fields, a scoring rubric, expected outputs, and the quick handoff artifacts for high-value non-bug feature asks.

Scope: apply to incoming enterprise feature asks that are not security incidents or urgent production defects. Work covers creation of the template, sample filled examples, triage rubric, a short runbook for CS to populate the skeleton during discovery calls, and a small dashboard (Google Sheet) for tracking requests through the first 3 stages: Intake -> Skeletonized -> Solution Sketched.

Objectives:
- Reduce noisy request payload by distilling asks into core user need + constraints + measurable success metrics.
- Produce an initial implementation sketch (API/console/infra touchpoints) suitable for an engineering pre-check within 3 business days.
- Standardize prioritization inputs so PMs can quickly compare cross-account asks using a consistent score.

Non-goals: full PRD, final estimates, formal security review, or production rollout planning (these happen after solution sketch acceptance).
triage_rubric: Strategic alignment (0-10) — product vision and roadmap fit; weight 3
Concentration of demand (0-10) — single-account vs multi-account; weight 2
Customer value / revenue impact (0-10) — ARR impact or retention risk; weight 3
Engineering complexity (0-10) — rough guess of infra/ui effort; weight 2 (lower is better)
Compliance friction (0-10) — presence of regulatory blockers; weight 2 (higher reduces score)
SLA / latency criticality (0-10) — special infra needs; weight 1
scoring_example: Example: Account X wants region-specific audit logs (scores: Strategic 8, Concentration 4, Revenue 7, Complexity 5, Compliance 9, SLA 2). Weighted total = (8*3)+(4*2)+(7*3)+(5*2)+(9*2)+(2*1) = 24+8+21+10+18+2 = 83. Interpretation: High priority for enterprise intake; escalate to engineering feasibility lane.
deliverables: Blank skeleton template (Google Form + sample responses)
Three anonymized example skeletons from recent CS asks
Solution sketch template (one-page): API endpoints, console changes, data/storage impact, rough infra notes
Triage scoring sheet (Google Sheet) with auto-weighted score
Runbook for CS to fill skeleton during discovery calls
Short Confluence guide linking to the above and to the engineering intake workflow
acceptance_criteria: Skeleton template exists and is accessible to Sales & CS
Runbook explains how to collect each template field and who to copy on submissions
At least 3 filled anonymized examples attached demonstrating edge cases (data residency, low-latency, console change)
Triage scoring sheet auto-calculates weighted priority and tags requests >=80 as 'engineering feasibility required'
Confluence guide published and shared in the Sales/CS weekly channel
risks: CS fills skeleton incompletely leading to low-quality sketches
Over-indexing on single large account requests and deprioritizing cross-account needs
Ambiguous 'solution sketch' language causing engineering rework
Security/compliance signals are surfaced late — escalate when present
runbook_quick_steps: 1) CS opens skeleton Google Form when an ask surfaces in a call
2) CS captures required fields and attaches any customer decks
3) PM on-call reviews within 48 hours and assigns a preliminary score
4) For score >=80, create a 'Solution Sketch' doc and request a 30-minute engineering pre-check
5) If engineering flags major blockers, mark customer and sales with risk notes and propose alternatives
